olivia: Customer reported an assistant confirmed a cancellation when they asked to 'suspend subscription' — acct acct_ABC123. Customer upset, billing impacted. Can we repro? :warning:

tara: Ugh. Do we have the assistant's function call payload or router logs?

olivia: Pasting the model function call we captured and the selector log:```json
{"model_call":{"tool_request":{"name":"suspend","args":{"user_id":"acct_ABC123","reason":"travel"}}}}
```
and router trace:```
[2026-06-01T14:12:03Z] selector-service decision: candidates=[pause_subscription(score=0.65), cancel_subscription(score=0.87)] chosen=cancel_subscription reason='alias_match' resolver=v1.3
[2026-06-01T14:12:03Z] callout -> cancel_subscription(args={"user_id":"acct_ABC123"})
```

kevin: Looks like a resolver alias collision. 'suspend' exists in cancel_subscription.aliases in current config. That explains the higher score despite user intent being temporary pause.

ada: This is a classic ambiguity between destructive vs non-destructive verbs. Our function-calling layer trusts the tool resolver ranking without intent disambiguation. We should: 1) prefer non-destructive candidate when intent contains words like 'temporary', 'pause', 'resume later'; 2) add an explicit confirmation step for any tool with metadata.destructive=true; 3) remove ambiguous single-word aliases like 'suspend' from cancel_subscription and map them explicitly to pause_subscription.

mohit: I can push a hotfix to selector-config: add explicit mapping 'suspend'->pause_subscription with higher priority and set metadata.destructive=true on cancel_subscription so the confirmation flow triggers. Rolling change now to staging then prod. ETA ~20m.

kevin: Also adding a unit test and an integration test to prevent regression. Repro curl for local test:```bash
curl -s -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/tools/resolve \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST' \
  -d '{"input":"suspend my subscription while I'm traveling","user_id":"acct_ABC123"}'
```
Expected resolver -> pause_subscription (confirm=false) not cancel_subscription.

olivia: Customer support updated the user that we are patching this now. They asked us to restore if any cancel happened by mistake — billing/team will handle restores. Marked P1.

deploy-bot: deploy started: selector-config v1.3.4 -> v1.3.5 (alias-priority patch). Instances: 6/6 rolling.

deploy-bot: deploy complete. smoke tests OK.

kevin: Patched selector to prefer non-destructive on 'suspend' and added confirmation middleware for destructive tools. Added telemetry event ambiguous_alias_hit. I opened a follow-up to audit all single-word aliases that map to destructive ops.

tara: Filing ticket PROD-1345 with notes and customer follow-up steps. Will confirm with billing if any unintended cancels need manual restore.

olivia: Thanks everyone — will update here after customer confirms. :thumbsup:
